case.case_title: Sirisena and Others v. Earnest Perera and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 14/90, decided on 7 May 1991

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the Petitioners were unlawfully detained without being brought before a judge or court as required by Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The Petitioners claimed they were detained unlawfully for several days without being produced before a judge or court and without legal authority.
case_context.respondent_argument: The Respondents denied unlawful detention and claimed the Petitioners were not detained but voluntarily attended police stations for questioning.
key_facts: 1st and 2nd Petitioners detained from 19 April to 22 April 1990 without being produced before a judge.
3rd to 5th Petitioners detained on 21 April 1990 and released the same day without court order.
No records or legal orders produced to justify detention.
Petitioners were not informed of any legal order authorizing their detention.
Respondents failed to produce detention register entries or affidavits from officers ordering release.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person deprived of liberty must be brought before a judge according to procedure established by law and cannot be further detained without a judge's order. This protects against unlawful detention.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Petitioners were detained for prolonged periods without being produced before a judge or court and without any legal order authorizing such detention. The Respondents' failure to produce records or affidavits corroborating lawful detention supported the finding of unlawful detention.
principles_established: Detention without production before a judge or legal order is unlawful under Article 13(2).
Police must follow procedure established by law for detention and produce detainees before a judge promptly.
Failure to produce detention records or legal orders undermines claims of lawful detention.
precedents_cited: State of Punjab v. Ajaib Singh AIR 1953 S.C. 10
Somawathie v. Weerasinghe S.C. Application No. 227/88

outcome.holding: The Court held that the Petitioners' fundamental rights under Article 13(2) were infringed by unlawful detention without being brought before a judge or court and without legal authority.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declarations of infringement, compensation awarded to Petitioners payable by the State and the 2nd and 3rd Respondents personally, and an inquiry ordered by the Inspector General of Police.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the Court's finding that the Petitioners were unlawfully detained without judicial oversight or legal order, violating their fundamental rights and entitling them to relief.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Petitioners were detained from 19 to 22 April 1990 without being produced before a judge or court and without any legal order authorizing their detention; Respondents failed to produce detention register entries or affidavits to justify detention.
